terms.name: Acid graphics
terms.definition: A 2020s rave revival style of chrome and liquid 3D objects, warped and stretched lettering, clashing saturated colour on near black, smileys, globes, and wireframe motifs.

terms.name: Anti-design
terms.definition: A deliberately awkward style that breaks layout, type, and color conventions so the interface reads as a statement rather than as a polished product.

terms.name: Atomic live region
terms.definition: A live region setting that makes assistive technology re-read the whole region when any part of it changes, instead of only the changed fragment.

terms.name: Bento grid
terms.definition: A grid whose cells are deliberately different sizes, tiled to fill a rectangle without gaps, like the compartments of a bento box.

terms.name: Brutalist web design
terms.definition: A raw style that leaves the document showing: system or monospace type, default link blue, hard borders, and no decoration beyond structure.

terms.name: Carousel
terms.definition: A row of items shown a few at a time that advances by arrows, swipe or a timer, with the rest waiting off screen.

terms.name: Chip
terms.definition: A compact, rounded element holding one value, which can usually be selected, removed, or both.

terms.name: Color gamut
terms.definition: The set of colours a space or a display can actually produce, which is why a value that is legal in one notation can be impossible on a given screen.

terms.name: Column resizer
terms.definition: The invisible strip on a column border that widens or narrows the column when dragged, and often fits the column to its content on double click.

terms.name: Consistent identification
terms.definition: Calling the same function by the same name and icon everywhere in a product, so a reader who learned it once does not have to relearn it per screen.

terms.name: Countdown timer
terms.definition: A running clock attached to an offer or a held resource, showing how long remains and what will happen when it reaches zero.

terms.name: Date picker
terms.definition: A field that opens a small calendar so a date can be chosen by looking at the month rather than typing it.

terms.name: Digital collage
terms.definition: A composition assembled from cut-out photography, torn paper edges, scanned texture, and type set at odd angles, so the page reads as pasted up rather than laid out.

terms.name: Double opt-in
terms.definition: Asking a new subscriber to confirm from the address they typed, so a list holds only addresses whose owner agreed and a typo never becomes a stranger's mail.

terms.name: Duration
terms.definition: How long a transition takes from start to finish, measured separately from the shape of its easing.

terms.name: Empty state
terms.definition: The screen a container shows when it holds nothing, naming the absence and offering the action that ends it.

terms.name: Faceted search
terms.definition: Narrowing results by ticking values from several independent attribute groups, with counts showing how many results each value would leave.

terms.name: Fill mode
terms.definition: Whether an animation's first or last keyframe styles apply outside its running window, which decides if an element snaps back when it finishes or stays where it landed.

terms.name: Fluid grid
terms.definition: A grid whose columns and gutters are expressed as proportions rather than fixed pixels, so the whole composition stretches and shrinks with its container.

terms.name: Follow-through
terms.definition: Parts of a composition that keep moving briefly after the main element stops, and start slightly after it starts, so a group does not move as one rigid block.

terms.name: Functional need
terms.definition: A statement of the gap between what a person can do and what a design demands, the WCAG 3 draft's way of naming a barrier without sorting people into disability categories.

terms.name: Gradual engagement
terms.definition: Replacing a sign-up form at the front door with a first useful action, so the reader experiences value before being asked for anything.

terms.name: Heading
terms.definition: A short line of type that names the section under it and, by its size and weight, says how far down the outline that section sits.

terms.name: Hover intent
terms.definition: Waiting out a short delay or watching cursor direction before acting on a hover, so a pointer merely passing through does not open anything.

terms.name: Images of text
terms.definition: Text baked into a raster image, which cannot be resized, restyled, selected, translated, or read by anything but the alt attribute someone remembered to write.

terms.name: Interpolation
terms.definition: The rule that produces the intermediate values between two endpoints, which is why some properties can animate smoothly and others can only switch.

terms.name: Kerning
terms.definition: The adjustment of space between two particular letters so the pair reads evenly.

terms.name: Layer cake pattern
terms.definition: A scanning shape where the eye reads headings and subheadings and skips the text between them, so the fixation map looks like stacked layers.

terms.name: Line drawing animation
terms.definition: An SVG stroke that appears to draw itself by animating its dash offset along its own length, used for signatures, check marks and illustrated line art.

terms.name: Long shadow
terms.definition: A flat era decoration where an icon casts a single hard shadow at 45 degrees that runs far past the shape before fading out.

terms.name: Media controls
terms.definition: The cluster of play, pause, skip, volume and fullscreen controls attached to a player, which usually hides itself while playing.

terms.name: Mini cart
terms.definition: A compact view of the basket opened from the cart icon, confirming what was just added and offering checkout without leaving the current page.

terms.name: Motion actuation
terms.definition: Triggering a function by moving the device itself, such as shake to undo, which needs a plain control alternative and an off switch.

terms.name: Navigation rail
terms.definition: A narrow vertical strip of top level destinations at the side of a screen, used at medium widths where a bottom bar is wasteful and a drawer is too heavy.

terms.name: Off canvas
terms.definition: Keeping secondary regions parked outside the viewport and sliding them in on demand, instead of stacking them below the main content.

terms.name: Organic blob
terms.definition: A soft irregular shape with no straight edges, used as a background accent or image mask to soften a strictly rectangular layout.

terms.name: Page transition
terms.definition: Motion that covers a navigation between two whole pages or routes, replacing the hard cut a document load would otherwise produce.

terms.name: Pilcrow
terms.definition: The paragraph mark, a reversed P with a doubled stem, used to show where a paragraph begins or as a hover anchor beside a heading.

terms.name: Positive tabindex
terms.definition: Using tabindex values above zero to force an order, which yanks those elements to the front of the whole page sequence and is almost always a bug.

terms.name: Progressive disclosure
terms.definition: Showing the few options most people need and keeping the rest one deliberate step away, so complexity arrives only when it is asked for.

terms.name: Quick view
terms.definition: Opening a summary of an item over the list it came from, so the reader can inspect it and return without losing scroll position or filters.

terms.name: Recurring event
terms.definition: An event stored once as a rule instead of as copies, so every second Tuesday can be edited, skipped for one week, or ended, without touching the rest.

terms.name: Ribbon
terms.definition: A tall tabbed toolbar that replaces menus, grouping commands into labelled sections with the important ones drawn larger.

terms.name: Saturation
terms.definition: How far a colour is from grey on a scale where 100 percent is the pure hue and 0 percent is neutral, as modelled by HSL and its relatives.

terms.name: Scroll spy
terms.definition: Navigation that watches the scroll position and highlights the entry for the section currently in view.

terms.name: Semantic color
terms.definition: A colour named for the job it does rather than the colour it is, so that "danger" or "surface" can be repointed without renaming anything that uses it.

terms.name: Signature pad
terms.definition: A drawing area that captures a handwritten signature by pointer or touch, with a clear control and a baseline to sign on.

terms.name: Smooth scrolling
terms.definition: Animating a programmatic jump so the page travels to its destination instead of cutting there, which keeps an anchor link or a back-to-top button from losing the reader's place.

terms.name: Speed dial
terms.definition: A floating action button that fans out into three to six smaller related actions when pressed or hovered.

terms.name: State layer
terms.definition: A translucent sheet of the content colour laid over a control at a fixed opacity per state, so hover, focus and pressed are one rule instead of three palettes.

terms.name: Structured format
terms.definition: Splitting one value across several small fields with fixed shapes, which teaches the expected format but costs the reader extra focus moves.

terms.name: Switch
terms.definition: A control shaped like a sliding track that turns one setting on or off and applies the change the moment it is flipped, with no separate save step.

terms.name: Tearsheet
terms.definition: A tall modal anchored to the bottom of the viewport that holds a multi step creation flow, stackable when one flow opens another.

terms.name: Tint
terms.definition: A colour with white mixed in, lighter than the original hue and used for faint fills, hover washes and subtle backgrounds.

terms.name: Tracking
terms.definition: The uniform space added to or removed from every letter across a run of text.

terms.name: Typewriter effect
terms.definition: Revealing text one character at a time, as if it were being typed, usually with a blinking caret trailing the last letter.

terms.name: Vertical rhythm
terms.definition: Spacing every block of text by multiples of one line height so the page keeps an even beat from top to bottom.

terms.name: Whitespace
terms.definition: The empty area between and around elements, treated as an active design material rather than as leftover space.

terms.name: Zero UI
terms.definition: A paradigm where the screen stops being the interface and the interaction happens through voice, gesture, presence, or sensors, so the system responds without anything to look at.
